The Hunnic {Mongol} Kings.
ineffably, for a period of six years.
They neglected the service of Arghun, the king of kings,
and became absorbed in the amassing of riches, mounts, gold, silver, and possessions.
Arghun, however, appointed other emirs to his service,
who rode with him, entered, went out, ate, and drank.
And everything that was administered in the camp and in the lands, both far and near,
they brought immediately to the attention of the king of kings,
saying, "Buqa acts haughtily toward the nobles and boasts,
and in obstinacy of will he does whatever he does."
And thus, all the affairs that Buqa established and built up,
these opposing emirs easily undermined and threw down before the king of kings.
Until three individuals from the nobles of Baghdad went to the royal camp
and made accusations against Aruq,
and showed that he was devastating and oppressing,
and had collected a great amount of wealth for himself through extortion.
Then the king of kings commanded
that these three individuals should be guarded with honor
until Aruq arrived at the camp.
Buqa {OCR?} sent and seized these men,
and cut off the heads of all three of them,
without interrogation, examination, or the permission of the judges.
And this was an open rebellion against the kingdom;
and through this deed, a great opening was made for the opponents of these two brothers, Buqa and Aruq.
And from then on, whatever was said concerning them
was easily and without hesitation accepted.
And the sons of the kings {OCR?: the royal princes} were deeply grieved over those who were killed,
and were very angry.
Buqa, however, pacified the mind {OCR?} of the princes with bribes,
and left and departed.
And a short time later,
a certain Jewish man named Sa'd al-Dawlah—
this man was the father-in-law of the governor of Baghdad—
because this governor passed away in those days,
that Jew approached the camp before the emirs and said,
"If you cancel the appointment of Aruq to Baghdad,
he will bring double the amount that used to be brought each year to the camp."
